record.context_brief: Asymptotic ratio of central to bicentral unlabeled trees.
record.original_question: Let c(n) and b(n) denote, respectively, the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled trees with n vertices. Does the ratio c(n) / b(n) tend to 1 as n tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE: Let c(n) and b(n) be the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled n-vertex trees, respectively. Then c(n)/b(n) -> 1 as n -> oo.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite tree T with at least one vertex, the eccentricity of a vertex v is the maximum distance from v to any other vertex of T. The center of T is the set of vertices of minimum eccentricity. It is a classical fact that the center of a tree consists of either exactly one vertex or two adjacent vertices; in the first case T is called central, and in the second case T is called bicentral.

For each integer n ≥ 1, let c(n) denote the number of central unlabeled trees on n vertices and b(n) the number of bicentral unlabeled trees on n vertices (so c(n) + b(n) equals the total number of unlabeled trees on n vertices).

Determine whether
  lim_{n → ∞} c(n) / b(n) = 1.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of the conjecture that the ratio of central to bicentral unlabeled n-vertex trees tends to 1. The asymptotic enumeration framework of Otter, Harary–Robinson–Schwenk, and Harary–Palmer gives precise asymptotics ~ C·ρ^{-n}·n^{-5/2} for various tree species, but no source explicitly confirms or refutes the limit c(n)/b(n) → 1. The current status appears to be unknown.

status_evidence.title: Twenty-step algorithm for determining the asymptotic number of trees of various species
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic enumeration framework for unlabeled trees of various species, including centered and bicentered trees.
status_evidence.claim: Provides asymptotic counts for various tree species but does not directly establish the ratio c(n)/b(n) → 1.

status_evidence.title: Central and Bicentral Trees
status_evidence.snippet: Definition: a tree is central if its center has one vertex, bicentral if its center has two adjacent vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the definitions of central and bicentral trees used in the conjecture.
